The Lifting Supervisor is responsible for overseeing and coordinating all lifting operations on site. This includes planning and preparing lifting activities involving tower cranes, mobile cranes, boom trucks, forklifts, gantry cranes, and related equipment. The role ensures all lifting tasks are performed safely, efficiently, and in full compliance with project requirements and regulatory standards. The Lifting Supervisor leads the lifting team and works closely with rigging personnel to assess conditions and guide proper execution of all lifting operations. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Health & Safety Responsibilities 
 Ensure all lifting equipment and materials are maintained in safe, operable condition, with all safety devices functional, calibrated, and properly certified.
 Enforce best practices in rigging and lifting techniques among all personnel.
 Maintain a consistently high standard of safety across all lifting activities.
 Verify that all required permits, documentation, and approvals are in place before lifting operations begin.
 Ensure all lifting equipment and devices comply with applicable Canadian standards and regulations in Ontario.
 Operational Responsibilities 
 Plan and prepare upcoming lifting activities, including equipment allocation, material requirements, task scheduling, and team dispatch in alignment with site priorities.
 Establish and implement clear procedures to ensure full understanding of lifting operations among lifting and logistics teams.
 Develop and enforce pre-start briefings and equipment-specific checklists for each type of machinery.
 Confirm that all operators and drivers complete required pre-shift equipment inspections.
 Conduct regular inspections of lifting devices to verify condition and readiness before each shift.
 Coordinate and organize lifting activities across all sites, ensuring efficient daily operation of lifting teams.
 Closely monitor the installation and operation of major equipment such as tower cranes, crawler cranes, and overhead cranes.
 Review and ensure strict adherence to approved lifting plans.
 Support equipment tracking and documentation of all Ontario Transit Group lifting devices.
 Maintain smooth team operations through proper planning of staffing, shift scheduling, and coverage.
 Collaborate closely with site engineers to ensure alignment of lifting activities with overall project goals.
 Perform daily on-site rounds to monitor team performance and provide coaching to improve skills.
 Adapt tasks and responsibilities as required throughout the duration of the project.
 Reporting Responsibilities 
 Ensure daily pre-start reports are completed and uploaded to the designated server.
 Collect and submit daily reports from site teams, including personnel attendance, hours worked, and tasks completed.
 Record hourly meters and/or kilometers of all on-site equipment (e.g., mobile cranes, heavy equipment) and provide updates to the Plant Engineer.
 Confirm that all lifting devices and equipment inspections are completed daily and forwarded to the Lifting Manager.
Minimum of 10+ years of experience within a construction-based Lifting Department, demonstrating a foundational understanding of lifting operations, site procedures, and safe equipment handling. Candidates with additional hands‑on exposure in heavy civil, industrial, or infrastructure projects will be considered an asset.
 Strong and up‑to‑date knowledge of lifting standards, regulations, and best practices, including safe rigging methods, equipment limitations, and compliance requirements relevant to construction environments.
 Valid Appointed Person Certification, confirming the ability to plan, supervise, and manage lifting operations while ensuring adherence to all safety protocols and legislative requirements.
 Proficiency in plant and logistics operations, including coordinating equipment movement, supporting site logistics planning, and ensuring efficient use of lifting assets across multiple work fronts.
 Demonstrated engineering and supervisory abilities, with the capacity to interpret technical documentation, review lifting plans, and oversee teams executing lifting and rigging tasks safely and effectively.
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, enabling clear direction to crews, coordination with site management, and effective collaboration with engineering, logistics, and HSE departments.
 Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and Outlook, with the ability to prepare reports, maintain equipment records, track documentation, and support daily operational administration.

Le/la PMCC Senior est un(e) expert(e) en gestion contractuelle, financière et des achats dans le domaine de la Construction et Mise en service (C&C). The Senior PMCC is an experienced professional in contractual, financial, and procurement management within Construction & Commissioning (C&C). With extensive experience in complex industrial and energy projects, the Senior PMCC serves as a mentor and subject matter expert, providing strategic guidance, sharing best practices, and supporting the professional development of other PMCCs. This role carries no direct managerial or operational responsibility for other PMCCs, who retain full accountability for their projects and decisions. 
 Job Description 
 Responsabilités principales
 1. Contrat et réclamations
 Agir comme expert de référence en gestion contractuelle, notamment sur les périmètres, exclusions, avenants et réclamations.
 Conseiller les PMCC sur les écarts contractuels et les stratégies de préparation des réclamations client.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques en matière de collecte de preuves, d'imputation des coûts et de documentation contractuelle.
 Apporter un soutien consultatif sur les situations contractuelles complexes, en collaboration avec les Directeurs de Projet et les Contract Managers.

 Fournir une expertise et des conseils sur le contrôle des budgets chantier, les prévisions financières et la distribution des coûts.
 Accompagner les PMCC dans l'identification des risques financiers, des écarts budgétaires et des mesures d'atténuation.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques pour la préparation des revues mensuelles (MPR/PMR).
 Contribuer à l'amélioration des méthodes et outils de suivi budgétaire.

 Fournir des conseils sur la préparation des Gate Reviews et les processus de mobilisation conformément aux standards GEV.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques concernant les budgets de mobilisation, la planification et la préparation des chantiers.
 Apporter une expertise sur les stratégies logistiques, les installations de chantier et les besoins en outillage (achat ou location).

 5. Pendant l'exécution du chantier
 Agir comme mentor et conseiller auprès des PMCC sur les enjeux rencontrés pendant l'exécution des chantiers.
 Fournir des recommandations sur la gestion des risques, des écarts budgétaires et des problématiques contractuelles.
 Promouvoir les meilleures pratiques en matière de sécurité, qualité, livraison et coûts.
 Faciliter le partage d'expérience sur la coordination entre les équipes de chantier, Engineering et Supply Chain.

 Conseiller les PMCC sur la préparation et la coordination des activités de mise en service.

 Apporter son expertise sur les interfaces entre construction et mise en service.

 Conseiller sur l'intégration des exigences EHS dans les SoW et les contrats de sous-traitance.
 Encourager l'identification proactive des risques et l'application des standards de sécurité GEV.
 8. Gouvernance et amélioration continue
 Agir comme référent métier et soutenir le développement des compétences des PMCC.
 Contribuer à l'amélioration des processus, outils et méthodes de gestion de projet C&C.

An overview of this role 
 As Manager, SOX PMO - Business Process, you'll lead Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance for assigned business processes as part of GitLab's second line. This is advisory work, not repeatable testing: you'll deeply understand how processes work, evaluate risks as the business changes, and help control owners design and remediate controls that hold up to audit. Judgment matters more than procedure. You'll form well-supported conclusions, align with control owners and Internal Audit, and defend positions to external auditors. GitLab already uses AI extensively, and the next phase brings AI agents into our SOX processes. You'll help teams adopt them with confidence, finding creative ways to enable new ways of working while maintaining compliance. You'll also partner with the information technology (IT) SOX PMO on readiness for new systems and applications. This role reports to the Senior Director, SOX PMO, within the Chief Accounting Officer's organization.
 What You’ll Do 
 Lead SOX compliance for assigned business processes as the second-line subject matter expert, advising control owners who own and operate the controls. Deeply understand each process, its systems and data flows, and resolve open questions and assumptions early.
 Monitor risks from new and changing processes, products, and systems. Help control owners design, strengthen, or right-size controls, and contribute to the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping.
 Evaluate control deficiencies individually and in aggregate, identify root causes, and prepare well-supported severity assessments. Work with management to develop, implement, and monitor remediation plans.
 Prepare auditor-ready technical memos on sampling methodology, scoping, and control rationalization, using independent analysis and sound conclusions. Prepare reports and presentations on SOX compliance status for leadership.
 Lead business walkthroughs and stakeholder meetings, and coordinate with Internal Audit and external auditors throughout the audit. Anticipate questions, support positions with data and judgment, and escalate risks and auditor comments promptly with a recommended path forward.
 Advise on controls for AI-enabled processes and processes that use AI agents. Find opportunities to automate SOX work using AI tools, and validate their output.
 Partner with the IT SOX PMO to assess new systems and controls, including application controls and key reports.
 Develop and maintain accurate process narratives, flowcharts, and risk and control matrices as processes change. Collaborate with Finance, Operations, Legal, Human Resources, Sales, Engineering, and IT leaders to help them design and maintain effective business controls.
 What You’ll Bring 
 Hands-on SOX and internal controls experience in control design, remediation, and deficiency evaluation, beyond testing alone. Experience in the software or technology industry is required; SOX PMO, Big Four risk advisory, or assurance experience is a strong plus.
 A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; an active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) credential (strongly preferred) or Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) credential.
 A strong understanding of SOX requirements and internal control frameworks, such as the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework.
 Professional judgment and skepticism: verifying facts against source documents, testing the reasonableness of data and conclusions, and recognizing missing information.
 A track record of independently solving ambiguous, novel problems, from defining an approach through overcoming obstacles and driving resolution. Curiosity to understand how processes actually work and keep learning as the business changes.
 Clear written and verbal communication, including concise, accurate, auditor-ready memos and actionable recommendations. Confidence partnering with senior stakeholders and external auditors, including working through pushback.
 A practical, innovative approach to helping the business adopt new technologies, products, and ways of working while maintaining compliance. Experience using AI tools to improve efficiency and validating their output.
 Experience with usage-based billing or AuditBoard is a plus.
 About the team 
 The SOX PMO is part of the Chief Accounting Officer's organization. In this role, you'll advise business control owners and partner with the IT SOX PMO, Internal Audit, and external auditors to keep GitLab compliant as processes, systems, and AI use evolve. GitLab is an all-remote company, with flexibility to work from home or wherever you're most productive. The Vice President, Enterprise Risk Management is a senior member of the CRO’s leadership team and serves as the CRO and Deputy CRO’s primary partner on enterprise risk governance, leading the second-line ERM function and the continued development and operation of a forward-looking risk management program aligned with regulatory expectations and commensurate with EQ Bank’s size, scope and complexity.

The VP, ERM will also lead the risk management aspects of integration of PC Financial with EQ Bank and build a high-performing ERM team that is nimble and innovative, enabling EQ Bank to achieve its strategic objectives while operating within its risk appetite.

Empowering Payroll Through Technology 
 At Manulife, we are transforming how our people experience work. Our PeopleComms Technology team enables simple, personalized and compliant experiences for colleagues around the world. We bring together deep business understanding, technology, data and emerging capabilities to help our People & Communications teams deliver their strategies at scale.
 As Manulife continues to build an AI-powered organization supported by digital-first integrated platforms and strong risk and governance, we are looking for leaders who can connect business ambition with technology execution.
 The Opportunity 
 Pay is one of the most personal and important experiences we deliver for colleagues. We are looking for a Payroll Technology Product Lead who will help shape how technology enables Payroll's evolving strategy, operations and colleague experience. 
 Working at the intersection of the Global People Services Rewards pillar and our enterprise Technology teams , you will be a strategic partner to Payroll leaders and the primary business-to-technology connector for the Payroll technology portfolio.
 You will develop a deep understanding of Payroll's priorities, processes and challenges and translate them into clear technology roadmaps, product requirements and delivery priorities. You will help move initiatives from business need through requirements, design, privacy and risk assessment, testing, implementation and continuous improvement.
 Just as importantly, you will look forward. You will monitor developments across Payroll technology, Workday, automation and AI and help the business understand where emerging capabilities could meaningfully improve colleague experience, strengthen controls, simplify processes or enable new ways of working, while keeping the process human where it matters most.
 This is not a traditional Payroll operations, project management or technology delivery role . You will be expected to connect strategy to technology, challenge assumptions, influence priorities and bring together business and technical teams to deliver sustainable solutions.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Shape the Payroll Technology Strategy and Roadmap 
 Partner with Payroll leaders to understand business strategy, operational priorities, colleague needs, regulatory requirements and opportunities for improvement.
 Translate Payroll priorities into a multi-year technology roadmap and investment priorities .
 Maintain a holistic view of the Payroll technology ecosystem, including dependencies across HCM, time, benefits, compensation, Finance and related enterprise platforms.
 Identify opportunities to simplify processes and make better use of existing enterprise platforms before introducing new solutions.
 Support business cases and recommendations for technology investments.
 Provide clear visibility into roadmap priorities, dependencies, decisions, risks and expected business outcomes.
 Translate Business Needs into Product Requirements 
 Serve as the connection point between Payroll and Technology throughout the product and delivery lifecycle.
 Lead discovery sessions to understand business problems, desired outcomes, process implications and colleague needs.
 Translate business needs into product requirements, business requirements, user stories, process flows and acceptance criteria .
 Partner with Technology teams, architects, business analysts and subject matter experts to evaluate solution options.
 Ensure proposed solutions address the original business need while supporting enterprise architecture, integration, scalability, security and supportability.
 Maintain and prioritize the Payroll technology product backlog in alignment with agreed business priorities.
 Enable Delivery and Business Acceptance 
 Represent Payroll throughout solution design, development and implementation.
 Coordinate business participation across system integration testing, user acceptance testing, regression testing and parallel payroll testing , where applicable.
 Define business acceptance criteria and ensure solutions are validated against intended business outcomes.
 Facilitate prioritization and resolution of defects and business decisions.
 Coordinate business sign-off and readiness for production.
 Partner with business and change teams to ensure new capabilities are understood, adopted and embedded into Payroll processes.
 Navigate Risk, Controls and Governance 
 Facilitate engagement with Privacy, Security, Risk, Compliance, Architecture and other governance partners as required.
Identify the privacy, security, risk, compliance, architecture and regulatory reviews required for Payroll technology initiatives, and coordinate timely engagement with the appropriate governance partners.
 Ensure technology initiatives appropriately consider payroll controls, sensitive colleague data, regulatory requirements, auditability and segregation of duties .
 Coordinate required business documentation and evidence through applicable governance processes. 
 Coordinate the completion of required assessments, approvals and supporting business documentation, ensuring decisions, conditions and evidence are recorded and traceable.
 Identify and escalate unresolved technology, business or control risks.
 Ensure decision rights and accountabilities remain clear across Payroll, PeopleComms Technology and enterprise Technology teams.
 Bring Emerging Technology into Payroll 
 Stay current on developments across Payroll technology, Workday, automation, AI and the broader HR technology ecosystem .
 Evaluate new functionality and emerging capabilities against real Payroll business problems and opportunities.
 Identify where AI and automation can improve the Payroll experience and where human judgment, care and accountability must remain, such as pay issues, exceptions and sensitive colleague situations.
 Proactively bring relevant recommendations to Payroll leadership.
 Partner with vendors and internal technology teams to understand roadmaps and influence future capability.
 Support experimentation and responsible adoption of emerging technology where there is a clear business case.
 Design AI-enabled solutions with appropriate human oversight so that decisions affecting colleagues' pay remain accountable, explainable and well controlled.
 Build Strong Partnerships 
 Build trusted relationships across Payroll, PeopleComms, Technology, Finance, Tax, Treasury, Risk and other enterprise partners.
 Translate complex Payroll needs for technical audiences and technology considerations for business audiences.
 Facilitate decisions and constructively challenge when business needs, technology constraints, cost, risk or timelines compete.
 Create clarity on priorities, ownership and decisions across highly matrixed teams.
 Represent Payroll technology priorities in relevant governance, planning and product forums.
 What Motivates You? 
 You are energized by solving complex business problems and enjoy working where business strategy and technology meet .
 You are equally comfortable working with a Payroll leader to understand an operational challenge and with Technology teams to determine how existing or emerging capabilities could solve it.
 You are curious about what is coming next, but you don't pursue technology for technology's sake. You ask what problem are we solving, what experience are we trying to create, and how will we know it is better? 
 You believe technology should make work simpler, and you know when a person, not a process, should be part of the moment.
 You thrive in a complex, global and regulated environment and are comfortable influencing outcomes where you may not directly own every team involved.
 Required Qualifications 
 5+ years of progressive experience in Payroll technology, HR technology, HRIS, product management, business analysis or large-scale HR transformation.
 Strong understanding of Payroll processes, controls and data , ideally within a complex, multi-jurisdictional organization.
 Demonstrated experience translating business strategy and requirements into technology solutions.
 Experience developing business requirements, product requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria .
 Experience supporting or leading UAT and end-to-end business testing for complex technology implementations or releases.
 Demonstrated ability to work across business, Technology, Risk, Privacy, Security and other control functions.
 Strong analytical, problem-solving and facilitation capabilities.
 Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex business and technology concepts for different audiences.
 Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and drive outcomes across highly matrixed teams.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with ADP GlobalView and ADP Celergo.
 Experience with Workday HCM or another large enterprise payroll platform.
 Experience supporting Payroll transformation, modernization or global payroll initiatives.
 Product management, product owner or business analysis experience.
 Experience with parallel payroll testing, integrations and complex end-to-end Payroll processes.
 Understanding of technology risk, privacy, security and regulatory requirements associated with employee and Payroll data.
 Experience evaluating or implementing automation, AI or emerging HR technology capabilities.
 Experience working within a global financial services or similarly regulated organization.
 When You Join Our Team 
 You'll join a team that is helping shape how technology enables the future of work at Manulife.
 You'll have the opportunity to influence one of our most important colleague experiences, work across business and Technology teams globally, and help determine how existing and emerging technology can enable Payroll to become simpler, more scalable and ready for the future.

About Clutch: 
 Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car-buying experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee… and that’s just the beginning.
 Named five years in a row to the Globe & Mail’s list of the Top Growing Companies in Canada and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50™ and Fast 500™ lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.
 Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, British Columbia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Canaan, Real Ventures, BrandProject, and Upper90. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.
 About the role: 
 Clutch is seeking a Facilities Supervisor to join our Facilities team, based at 3350 Wolfedale Road in Mississauga with regular travel to our GTA sites. This is a hands-on, technically capable leadership role: you plan the work, run the team, and make sure the work gets done. You’ll own maintenance planning across Clutch’s sites, run our CMMS day to day, manage the vendors we contract for specialized work, and hold the day and night teams to clear standards. You’ll lead a team spanning entry-level Technician I to skilled Technician II, act as the technical escalation point above Technician II, and report to the Director of Facilities.
 What you’ll do: 
 Plan and schedule the work – build and run the preventive maintenance (PM) program for every site in the CMMS (assets, frequencies, checklists, tour routes), plan daily and weekly work for the day and night teams at the right level for each role, and prioritize work orders by safety, operational impact, and cost, including seasonal work, projects, and new site launches
 Lead the team – supervise the Building Maintenance Technicians (I and II, days and nights) and cleaning staff: set expectations, assign work, follow up and inspect, and review night tours, tickets, logged time, and handoff notes every morning
 Coach and develop – run documented training plans, daily huddles, and a weekly planning meeting, and grow Technician I team members toward the Technician II level; manage schedules, attendance, time approvals, overtime, and performance reviews with HR support
 Own the CMMS and reporting – keep it as the single system of record (all work ticketed, all time logged, all tours completed) and report weekly to the Director on PM completion, overdue work, response times, and vendor activity
 Troubleshoot building systems – HVAC and makeup air, plumbing, electrical, doors, pumps, pressure washers, air compressors, drains, and oil-water separators – backing up Technician II on complex faults and acting as technical escalation, including for after-hours emergencies
 Manage vendors – coordinate contracted trades and the cleaning contractor, verify work before closing tickets, track vendor cost and performance, and bring work in-house where the team has the skill
 Keep the team safe – maintain safe work practices (lockout/tagout, PPE, working at heights, WHMIS, hazardous waste) and the after-hours escalation call tree, and coordinate maintenance at our Nova Scotia and British Columbia sites through local contacts and vendors
 Pitch in when it counts – in severe weather, emergencies, or site launches, all Facilities team members may be asked to help outside their usual tasks, sites, or hours
 What we’re looking for: 
 Experience: 5+ years in building maintenance or facilities operations in a commercial, industrial, or automotive setting, including 2+ years supervising a maintenance team
 Planning: Proven experience planning and scheduling maintenance work and running a PM program
 Technical knowledge: Strong working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems, and the judgment to know when a licensed trade is needed
 Systems: Hands-on CMMS experience (work orders, PM scheduling, assets, reporting) and proficiency in Google Workspace
 Leadership: Plans ahead, holds people accountable fairly and consistently, and communicates clearly with the team, vendors, and leadership
 License: Full (unrestricted) G driver’s licence (or provincial equivalent) and a clean driving record (driver’s abstract required)
 Background Check: Clean criminal record check
 Work Authorization: Legally authorized to work in Canada
 Nice to have: College diploma or trade certificate in a building-related field; Building Environmental Systems (BES) or similar; First Aid/CPR, WHMIS, Working at Heights, and lockout/tagout certifications
 This is a fully on-site role with regular travel between GTA sites. It’s physical work, including lifting up to 50 lbs, climbing ladders, and working in mechanical spaces.

 À propos de l'employeur 
 S'installer au Canada, ce n'est pas juste changer de pays. C'est aussi choisir un endroit où on a envie de travailler tous les jours.
 Ici, c'est une auberge-restaurant installée dans une maison ancestrale, sur la Côte-de-Beaupré, face au fleuve Saint-Laurent. Vingt minutes de Québec, dix minutes du Mont-Sainte-Anne. L’Analyste des systèmes d’affaires (BSA) - Salesforce agit comme un lien entre les besoins d’affaires et la solution technique Salesforce. Il ou elle analyse les processus, définit les exigences fonctionnelles et soutient la mise en œuvre, le maintien et l’amélioration continue des systèmes d’affaires de l’entreprise.
 Il s'agit d'un poste temporaire de 12 mois avec une possibilité de passer en permanent par la suite. 
 Responsabilités : 
 Recueillir, analyser et documenter les besoins d’affaires et les exigences système avec les parties prenantes.
 Traduire les besoins en exigences fonctionnelles et non fonctionnelles et définir des critères de succès mesurables.
 Analyser et optimiser les processus « as-is » / « to-be » et les modéliser avec BPMN, Visio ou outils similaires.
 Produire et maintenir la documentation d’analyse : BRD, FRD, User Stories, Use Cases, RTM, Fit-Gap, analyses d’impacts, CAB et documentation d’ateliers.
 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes, architectes et développeurs à la conception de solutions évolutives alignées aux objectifs d’affaires.
 Gérer la roadmap des produits et solutions et identifier les opportunités d’amélioration continue.
 Coordonner le cycle de vie des applications : maintenance, mises à niveau, fournisseurs, sécurité, performance et améliorations.
 Animer les ateliers, rencontres et comités décisionnels et assurer la collaboration entre les différentes équipes.
 Soutenir l’assurance qualité : plans et cas de tests, UAT, validation des exigences et gestion des anomalies.
 Contribuer aux intégrations système : interfaces, mappage et validation des données, qualité et intégrité des données.
 Soutenir la gestion du changement: analyse d’impacts, préparation, formation et transfert des connaissances.
 Assurer le soutien applicatif N3 et coordonner les escalades N4 avec les fournisseurs et équipes de développement.
 Suivre la performance des solutions, recommander des améliorations et contribuer à la gouvernance et à la création de valeur.
Pour vous joindre à notre équipe: 
 Minimum de 5 ans d'expérience à titre d'analyste d'affaires, d'analyste des systèmes d'affaires ou d'analyste fonctionnel.
 Bilinguisme (français et anglais), à l'oral comme à l'écrit
 Compétences et outils utilisés : 
 Bonne connaissance de Salesforce
 Outils de gestion des exigences et de collaboration: Confluence, Azure DevOps
 Modélisation et cartographie des processus: Microsoft Visio
 Documentation: Suite Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) et SharePoint
 Outils de données: Connaissances de base en SQL et des outils de rapports décisionnels (BI) (un atout)
 Méthodologies : Agile, Scrum et Waterfall
Ce que nous offrons! 
 Un salaire annuel concurrentiel, des vacances, des avantages sociaux et un programme de contrepartie REER
 Programme annuel de bourses pour frais de scolarité de l'AIM jusqu'à 8 500 $ par personne à charge admissible
 Les outils et le soutien nécessaires pour réussir dans votre carrière et votre perfectionnement professionnel

ABOUT VENN

Venn is building the business banking Canadian companies should already have. For decades, business owners here have banked with institutions that were slow, expensive and not built for them. Venn gives them multi-currency accounts, global transfers, corporate cards and AI finance tools in one place, so they spend less time on their finances and more on their business.

Our founders both worked at Revolut before starting Venn and were raised by small business owners. Today more than 15,000 Canadian businesses run on Venn. We're the fastest-growing B2B fintech in Canada, and we ranked 10th among Canada's fastest-growing companies by revenue in 2026. Backed by Left Lane Capital, Gradient, Intact Ventures and XYZ Venture Capital we're Series A and have raised $26.5M to date.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Principal Product Designer, you'll help set the design direction for the product thousands of Canadian businesses use to run their finances. You'll own how our core product areas work and fit together, lead the evolution of our design system, and partner directly with our co-founder, who leads product and engineering, on what we build next. This is a hands-on role for a designer who wants to shape strategy and still ship the work.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own design direction across core areas of the Venn platform, including accounts, cards, payments and expense management, and how they come together as one product.

 - Partner with our co-founder and product leadership on product direction and roadmap, shaping what we build as well as how it works.

 - Own the evolution of our design system, setting the patterns and standards the whole product is built on.

 - Take ambiguous, zero-to-one problems from an open question to shipped product, staying hands-on through flows, prototypes and final production design.

 - Set the bar for craft and quality across design, leading critique and giving clear, direct feedback.

 - Mentor other designers and help hire as the design team grows.

 - Work closely with engineering to make sure what ships matches what was designed.

 - Use customer insight, data and feedback to decide where design can have the most impact, and iterate on shipped work against real usage.


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 8+ years of product design experience, including time at Staff, Principal or Lead level.

 - A portfolio of complex products you shaped from strategy through to shipped detail.

 - A track record of building or significantly evolving a design system.

 - Experience designing financial products or similarly complex B2B software.

 - Experience working directly with founders or senior leadership at a startup or high-growth company.

 - Exceptional interaction and visual design craft, with deep fluency in Figma.

 - Strong product judgment and the ability to focus on what matters most.

 - Clear communication that brings product, engineering and leadership along with your thinking.

 - Comfort prototyping in code or with AI tools.


BONUS POINTS

 - Experience at a fintech, in banking, payments, cards or spend management.

 - Experience as an early design hire, building a design practice as the company scaled.

 - Experience mentoring and hiring designers.



How we work. We raise the bar, own the outcome, challenge assumptions, win as one and move fast. In practice that means honest feedback, continuous iteration, and decisions grounded in data.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Equity in a Series A company, so you share in the growth you help build.

 - Health, dental and vision benefits from your first day.

 - Four weeks of vacation.

 - Unlimited sick / personal days

 - Paid parental leave top up

 - Weekly lunches and paid dinners when work goes late
   
   

This posting is for an existing vacancy. We use AI tools in our process but people make every hiring decision. Venn is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by law. Accommodations are available at any stage on request. We only contact candidates from an @venn.ca http://venn.ca email or Ashby and will never ask for payment or banking details.



If you want to build the business banking Canadian companies run on, Venn is the place to do it. Meet most of the requirements but not every one? Apply anyway.

 Notre façon de travailler 
 Nous accompagnons chaque projet de bout en bout, de l'offre de service à la clôture. Nous croyons à l'intelligence collective et à la collaboration, avec les valeurs de Norda Stelo : confiance, excellence, intégrité, respect, innovation et adaptabilité. 
 Notre ambition 
 Être le partenaire privilégié de nos équipes de vente et de projet : des offres de service mieux préparées pour remporter des mandats rentables, et des projets mieux soutenus pour les livrer avec confiance.

 Assurer une vision globale de la performance financière : consolider, analyser et interpréter les données financières de l'ensemble du portefeuille afin d'offrir une lecture claire de la santé des projets.

 Garantir la qualité de l'information : effectuer des vérifications ciblées afin d'assurer l'exactitude, la cohérence et la fiabilité des données financières et des prévisions.

 Automated Credit Strategy are TD's primary frameworks used to assess new small business credit applications. The strategies rely on a combination of policy rules, customer and business information, bureau data, and legacy risk grid, which segments applicants into risk categories based on predefined score thresholds and decision rules. 
 To further modernize credit adjudication and support portfolio growth TD has developed Atlas, a machine learning-based Probability of Default (PD) model designed specifically for the small business clients. Atlas leverages a significantly broader set of predictive variables than the traditional models. The model provides a more sophisticated assessment of credit risk and has demonstrated stronger predictive performance than legacy scorecard-based approaches.

Decision cutoffs would be calibrated to ensure alignment with TD's risk appetite while maximizing automation and responsible growth opportunities. About Tailscale 
 About the Role 
 We are seeking a Product Manager to own Tailscale's networking features — the layer that decides how traffic finds its destination by name on top of Tailscale’s seamless mesh connectivity solution. Concretely, you will own four feature sets: App Connectors , DNS , Funnel , and Tailscale Serve & Services .
 A tailnet gives every device an identity and an address. Networking features are what turn addresses into something a person, a script, or an AI agent can actually use — a name, a service, an app, a URL.
 App Connectors route traffic to specific SaaS and private applications by name, so access follows the app rather than the IP.
 DNS — MagicDNS, split DNS, custom name servers, search domains
 Tailscale Serve & Services make a workload — not a machine — the unit of connectivity and access: addressable, load-balanced, and durable across the instances behind it. This is the wedge that lets customers replace a service registry, and eventually much of what they use a service mesh for, with Tailscale.
 Funnel is Tailscale's ingress story: securely exposing a Service running inside the tailnet to the public internet, from a hobbyist sharing a dev server to production webhooks and public endpoints.
 This is the most user-visible role in Tailscale's Dataplane Platform, and the work is as much product design as it is networking. DNS settings, connector topologies, and service definitions are configured by network engineers and IT admins in the admin console, API, and CLI, and the distance between "magical" and "unusable" is the object model, the defaults, and the error messages. 
 See How Tailscale Works , Tailscale Funnel , and Four ways to Tailscale a service to learn more.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Tailscale's networking features: App Connectors, DNS, Funnel, and Tailscale Services
 Own the operator experience across these surfaces: how network engineers and IT admins configure, segment, monitor, and troubleshoot them at scale, in both the admin console and the CLI
 Partner with GTM, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering on production commitments and strategic deals, and champion the migration path from reverse proxies, bastion hosts, cloud ingress, and service meshes to Tailscale
 Build systematic customer insight across the full spread of Tailscale users, from a homelab operator exposing a media server through Funnel to a large enterprise replacing its service registry
 What We Are Looking For 
 7+ years in product management, including direct ownership of an application-layer connectivity product: reverse proxies, ingress controllers or gateways, API gateways, service mesh or service registry, DNS and traffic management, secure tunneling and exposure products, or identity-aware proxy connectors
 A track record of turning a complex networking system into a legible product surface: you can point to an object model, a set of defaults, or a configuration experience you designed and explain why it was right
 End-to-end ownership of a product area: strategy, requirements, launch (docs, enablement, rollout), and the iteration after launch
 Evidence of data-informed decisions — metrics you defined, instrumentation you pushed for, and at least one time the data changed your mind
 Nice To Have

 Kubernetes networking: ingress, Gateway API, operators, or service exposure patterns
 Hands-on experience with secure tunneling and exposure products (ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Access, Teleport, Zscaler Private Access) as a builder or a heavy user
 Abuse prevention, rate limiting, or trust and safety work on a publicly exposed service
